global_rule.definition: A major top is a mountain peak with a substantial rise before it and a substantial fall after it. Nearby plateau peaks are not separate majors. Once a major top establishes the level, later accepted peaks must be at the same level or higher.
global_rule.right_edge: Include an extreme-right high provisionally when it extends the established peak line even though a future decline cannot yet confirm it.
global_rule.plateau_shelf: Do not retain an older low-level shelf merely because it has large percentage prominence; it must still read as a major peak in the active ceiling regime.
global_rule.two_sided_confirmation: A confirmed top needs a meaningful valley on both sides. If price reaches a higher level before falling, the lower candidate is a shoulder on the same mountain and must be removed.
global_rule.rise_fall_sharpness: Depth alone is insufficient. The rise into a major top and the rejection after it must be steep; among comparable-level candidates, prefer the sharper mountain and discard the slower weaker one.
global_rule.chart_scale_relevance: Ignore locally valid swings that sit too low in the active ten-year price range. A major top must be visually material relative to the full chart, not merely prominent relative to a small local base.
global_rule.active_line_classification: Breakout and setup classification must use the reviewed active major-top line. An older historical resistance fit can falsely label a current good setup as already broken out.
global_rule.interval_native_confirmation: For a 3M chart, the significant fall after a peak must occur in a later 3M candle. A monthly high and crash inside the same quarterly candle cannot confirm that candle as a major top.
global_rule.minimum_line_anchors: Always plot at least two meaningful, well-separated ceiling anchors when the chart has enough history. If only one strict major mountain survives, add the strongest comparable structural retest so the lid has a measurable slope for coil grading.
global_rule.intermediate_line_retests: Once two well-separated endpoint anchors define a lid, retain a meaningful intermediate pivot that closely retests that same line. This can produce a three-touch flat lid even when the middle point is not independently strict enough to be a primary mountain.
